Bayesian landscape-scale fits

Source: R/doc_bayes_class.R
multiScaleR_bayes-class.Rd

multiScale_bayes() returns an object of class multiScaleR_bayes. It is a list that holds the frozen model, the parameter layout, and, once a method has been run, the posterior draws and the record of that computation. This page lists every element, shows where each model parameter lives and on which scale, explains how to convert it to a distance or a multiplier, and names the functions that read the object. The Bayesian interface is experimental. Printing any of these objects reports "Experimental Bayesian landscape-scale model".

Elements in every object

  • specification: the frozen model. Rows, landscape bins, formulas, priors, and the reference standardization are fixed here once and reused by every method. See "Read the specification".

  • parameters: a named list of seven numeric vectors that defines the parameter layout and holds starting values. It contains no estimates. See "Find each parameter".

  • call: the matched call to multiScale_bayes().

  • inference: a label for the computation, one of "prepared", "full Bayesian NUTS", "full Bayesian slice sampling", "joint Laplace Gaussian approximation", "marginal Laplace with scale-SD quadrature", or "importance-corrected marginal Laplace".

  • inference_metadata: a description of what the object estimates. See "Read the inference metadata". Fits saved by older versions of the package can lack it, and they remain usable.

Elements added by each method

methodElements added
"prepare"None. There are no draws, so the object cannot be used for posterior summaries or prediction
"sample" (NUTS)draws, sampler, sampling, diagnostics
"slice"draws, chains, sampling, diagnostics
"laplace"draws, laplace, diagnostics
"marginal"draws, marginal, diagnostics
"marginal" with correction = "importance"draws, marginal, importance, diagnostics

  • draws: a named list of seven numeric matrices, one per parameter block in the order of parameters. Each matrix has one row per retained joint posterior vector and one column per parameter in the block, on the internal scales given in "Find each parameter". Row i of every block belongs to the same joint vector, so compute derived quantities from whole rows. NUTS rows come in permuted order. Slice rows follow the chains, one chain after another. Laplace and marginal rows are independent draws from the approximation. Importance-corrected rows are resampled, with replacement, from the weighted candidates.

  • sampler (NUTS): the stanfit object returned by tmbstan.

  • chains (slice): a numeric array of post-warmup iterations by chains by parameters, with parameter names such as "beta[1]" and "scale_beta[1]". Chain diagnostics and bayesplot chain plots read it.

  • sampling (NUTS and slice): the chains, iter, warmup, seed, and effective cores used. NUTS also records control and laplace = FALSE.

  • laplace, marginal, importance: records of the approximations. See "Read the approximation records".

  • diagnostics: the numerical checks of the computation. See "Read the stored diagnostics".

Find each parameter

The seven parameter blocks appear in the same order in parameters, specification$parameters, draws, and every concatenated vector or matrix (the Laplace mode, covariance, and hessian, the importance candidates, and the columns of chains).

BlockOne entry perWhat it holdsScale storedInterpretable form
betaname in specification$beta_namesResponse coefficientsLink scaleRead directly, or exp() for count and binomial models. Summarized in summary(fit)$coefficients
scale_betacolumn of each scale designScale-formula coefficientsLog of distance divided by specification$unit_conv for intercepts and ~0 + year coefficients. Log-distance contrasts for the restAdd log(unit_conv) to the intercepts to get log map units, then exp() for a distance. exp() of a contrast is a ratio of distances. Summarized in summary(fit)$scale_coefficients
scale_zlevel of each scale grouping termStandardized group deviations with a standard-normal priorNoneMultiply by the group SD to get the deviation in log scale
log_scale_sdscale random-intercept termLog of the between-group SD of log scale (tau)Logexp() gives tau. exp(tau) is a multiplier on the scale. Summarized in summary(fit)$group_sd$log_scale_group_sd
response_zlevel of each response grouping termStandardized random intercepts with a standard-normal priorNoneMultiply by the response group SD to get the intercept on the link scale
log_response_sdresponse random-intercept termLog of the random-intercept SDLog of a link-scale SDexp(). Summarized in summary(fit)$group_sd$response_group_sd
log_dispersionNB2 or Gaussian model (empty otherwise)Log NB2 size theta, or log Gaussian residual SDLogexp(). Summarized in summary(fit)$dispersion

The link scale is the log expected count for Poisson and NB2 models, the log odds for binomial models, and response units for Gaussian models.

Each landscape predictor's scale for observation i, in map units, is

$$\log D_i = x_i^\top b + \sum_k \exp(s_k) z_{k, g_k(i)} + \log(u)$$

where \(x_i\) is row i of the scale design specification$scales[[name]]$X, \(b\) is scale_beta[specification$scales[[name]]$beta_index], \(s_k\) is the entry of log_scale_sd for random term \(k\), \(z_{k, g}\) is the entry of scale_z for group \(g\), and \(u\) is specification$unit_conv. Within specification$scales[[name]]$random, each term records z_index (positions in scale_z, one per level in levels), index (each row's level), and sd_index (position in log_scale_sd). Response random terms in specification$response$random use the same fields for response_z and log_response_sd. This noncentered form, a standard-normal deviation times a group SD, is the coordinate system the samplers and approximations work in.

For a shared scale, exp(scale_beta + log(unit_conv)) is the scale itself. For ~1 + (1 | year), the same expression gives the typical scale, the median of the population distribution of annual scales, and tau is exp(log_scale_sd). A year one SD above typical has a scale exp(tau) times the typical one. posterior_scales() performs these conversions for every distinct combination of scale covariates and groups. Prefer it to rebuilding them by hand.

Read the specification

specification is a list. Most users need only a few elements.

  • covariates: names of the landscape predictors whose scales are estimated. kernel is "gaussian" or "exp".

  • unit_conv: the distance normalizer of the prepared inputs. Internal log scales are in units of distance divided by unit_conv.

  • support: min_D and max_D of the prepared inputs, in map units. They are a reference range for posterior_scales(), not bounds on the prior.

  • center, spread: the fixed reference standardization of each landscape predictor, computed once across fitting rows at the prior median scale. A response coefficient refers to one spread unit of the kernel-weighted predictor at that scale.

  • priors: the complete prior settings, with defaults filled in. scale_median is a named vector, one entry per landscape predictor.

  • beta_names: the names of the response coefficients, in beta order.

  • scales: one list per landscape predictor, holding the scale formula, its design matrix X, beta_index, distance_location (TRUE for coefficients that are log distances rather than contrasts), the prior mean and SD of each coefficient (prior_mean, prior_sd, on the internal log scale), random terms, and labels with the representatives rows used to report each distinct combination.

  • response: the response formula, its model frame, terms, random terms, and the levels and contrasts retained for prediction.

  • family, y, trials, offset: the response family, the response vector (successes for binomial data), the binomial trial totals (1 for other families), and the offset.

  • data, rows, observation_ids, row_id: the observation data, the prepared landscape row of each observation, its point ID, and the name of the row-ID column (NULL when row names were used). Older saved fits can lack row_id.

  • V, C, delta: binned value sums, finite-cell counts, and shifted distance terms for kernel means.

  • X_fixed: the design columns that do not involve a landscape predictor.

Some models add response_design (interactions and expressions that involve a landscape predictor), surface (weighted SQ buffers, their specifications, and the memory planning record), or fixed_reference (the preparation normalization of declared fixed-radius metrics).

Read the inference metadata

inference_metadata describes the target and the treatment of uncertainty. It does not report whether a fit passed its checks.

  • schema_version: version of this structure.

  • target: always "posterior" for these objects.

  • method: "prepare", "nuts", "slice", "joint_laplace", "marginal_laplace", or "importance_corrected".

  • objective: "negative_log_posterior". population_priors is "proper", because every parameter has a prior. response_normalizers is "retained".

  • integration: how scale effects, response effects, and population parameters (group SDs) are treated, such as "joint_sampling", "joint_gaussian", or "joint_importance_sampling", or "not_computed" for a prepared object.

  • solver: "none", "nuts", "slice", "optimization", or "importance_sampling".

  • uncertainty: intervals is "marginal_credible" once fitted and "not_provided" when prepared. population_parameters and annual_scales state that group-SD uncertainty is propagated through the joint posterior. calibration is always "not_established", because no method has demonstrated interval coverage for general data sets.

  • diagnostics_field: the name of the element that holds the checks, "diagnostics". metadata_establishes_eligibility is always FALSE.

Read the stored diagnostics

Every fit has diagnostics$passed (TRUE, FALSE, or NA) and, in most cases, criteria, a sentence stating the rule applied. The other fields depend on the method.

MethodFieldspassed requires
NUTSparameters (a posterior summary table with rhat, ess_bulk, ess_tail), divergences, max_treedepth_hits, ebfmi (one per chain)At least 2 chains, Rhat at most 1.01, bulk and tail effective sample size at least 100 per chain, no divergences or tree-depth hits, and E-BFMI at least 0.3
SliceparametersThe same chain rules, without the NUTS-only checks. Without the posterior package, passed is NA, parameters is NULL, and reason explains why
Laplacetype, gradient_max, min_eigenvalue, condition_number, competing_modes, successful_starts, startsNo distinct mode within 2 log-posterior units. A failed optimizer or an invalid Hessian stops the fit instead
Marginaltype, grid_converged, grid_nodes, refinement, competing_mass, upper_tail_mass, gradient_max, condition_numberA converged grid, competing_mass at most 0.01, and upper_tail_mass at most 0.001
Importancepareto_k, ess, min_tail_ess, max_weight, split_cdf_error, type, candidates, min_candidates, proposal_df, production_candidates, proposal_passedPareto k at most 0.7, ess at least 1000, min_tail_ess at least 400, max_weight at most 0.01, and split_cdf_error at most 0.05

In the importance checks, ess measures how concentrated the weights are, min_tail_ess the precision of tail indicators, pareto_k the presence of extreme ratios, max_weight dominance by one candidate, and split_cdf_error the disagreement between two independent halves of the production candidates. min_candidates is the requested minimum.

For the samplers, these checks cover the raw parameters. Use diagnose_bayes_scales() to check the scales and group SDs you report. For the approximations, a passed check says the arithmetic finished cleanly. It does not say the approximation is close to the posterior. vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR") explains each check and what to do when one fails.

Read the approximation records

Modes, covariances, Hessians, and candidates in these records use the unconstrained, noncentered coordinates of "Find each parameter", with the blocks concatenated in order.

  • laplace: mode, the joint covariance and hessian at the mode, every optimizer attempt in starts, the selected_start, and the number of draws, seed, cores, and a coordinates note. The covariance keeps correlations among coefficients, scales, and group SDs.

  • marginal: the integration grid over the one scale-group SD. x holds the nodes in the coordinates of the SD's half-normal prior CDF (0 to 1). weights, density, cumulative, and log_normalizer describe the integrated SD distribution at those nodes. nodes holds the conditional approximation at each node, with its mode, covariance, hessian, log_density, and optimizer attempts. The record also keeps prior_sd, the grid refinement history, converged, hyper_index (the position of the SD), parameter_indices (positions of node parameters in the full layout), and the draws, seed, cores, control, and coordinates used. With one response grouping term integrated inside an importance-corrected fit, the nodes exclude its latent site effects. The log normalizer describes the numerical integration. It is not a model-selection criterion.

  • importance: all retained production candidates (one row each) with normalized weights and log_weights (log posterior minus log proposal density), and the resample_ids into the candidates that built draws. history has one row per production stage, with its diagnostics, whether it passed, and whether it met the requested minimum (budget_met). The record also keeps the seed, a text description of the proposal, the adapted_proposal mixture (its components and their weights, where each learned component counts in skipped_nodes the nodes that kept their original geometry), pilot_candidates, proposal_indices, the conditional_response flag, production_candidates (including discarded stages), response_proposal (fallback count and largest remaining Newton step), and proposal_diagnostics, the original marginal checks. target_evaluation counts every posterior density evaluation (evaluations), invalid automatic-differentiation values (ad_invalid), ordinary rechecks that recovered a finite or zero density (recovered_finite, recovered_zero), and values left unresolved, including pilots and discarded stages. Every candidate is kept, and unresolved densities still fail the importance checks. With conditional_beta = TRUE the record also holds conditional_beta and beta_proposal, which gives the starting coefficients (start), the number of fallbacks to the coefficients' normal prior, the largest remaining Newton step (max_step), and the latent_prior_fraction of the defensive component.

Functions that read a fit

FunctionWhat it returns
print()Family, observations, scale formulas, and the stored diagnostic status
summary()Coefficients, scales, scale coefficients, group SDs, dispersion, and diagnostics. See multiScale_bayes()
posterior_scales()Each scale in map units or log map units, with mass below min_D and above max_D
plot.multiScaleR_bayes()Interval plots of scales or group SDs
diagnose_bayes_scales()Chain diagnostics and Monte Carlo error for scales and group SDs (needs chains or sampler)
diagnose_bayes_probabilities()Probabilities that scales fall below thresholds, with Monte Carlo error
diagnose_bayes_laplace()A reweighted check of scale probabilities from an uncorrected approximation
predict.multiScaleR_bayes()Expected responses or linear predictors at fitted or new observations
predict_scales()Scales at new scale covariates and groups, including unsurveyed years
simulate.multiScaleR_bayes()Posterior predictive replicate responses
simulate_bayes_prior()Prior predictive responses and scales (a prepared object is enough)
plot_marginal_effects()Coefficient effect curves at the fixed reference standardization
cross_validate_bayes()Refits the model in each fold and scores held-out observations

aic_tab() and bic_tab() do not accept these objects.

See also

multiScale_bayes(), posterior_scales(), predict.multiScaleR_bayes(), diagnose_bayes_scales(); vignette("v13-bayesian-scales", package = "multiScaleR") for fitting and reading a model, vignette("v14-bayesian-prediction", package = "multiScaleR") for prediction, and vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR") for the computation methods and their diagnostics.

Examples

# A stored slice-sampling fit with one shared scale per landscape layer
cache <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-bayesian-scales.rds",
                             package = "multiScaleR"))
fit <- cache$fit
fit$call                       # the call that produced this fit
#> multiScale_bayes(formula = counts ~ site + land1 + land2, inputs = inputs, 
#>     data = landscape_counts, family = "poisson", priors = list(scale_median = c(land1 = 300, 
#>         land2 = 300)), method = "slice", seed = 5211)
lengths(fit$parameters)        # 4 coefficients and 2 scale intercepts
#>            beta      scale_beta         scale_z    log_scale_sd      response_z 
#>               4               2               0               0               0 
#> log_response_sd  log_dispersion 
#>               0               0 
fit$specification$beta_names   # order of the beta columns
#> [1] "(Intercept)" "site"        "land1"       "land2"      
dim(fit$chains)                # iterations x chains x parameters
#> [1] 1000    4    6

# Rebuild sigma for land1, in meters, from whole rows of the draws
sm <- fit$specification$scales$land1
log_sigma <- fit$draws$scale_beta[, sm$beta_index] +
  log(fit$specification$unit_conv)
quantile(exp(log_sigma), c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))
#>     2.5%      50%    97.5% 
#> 180.7061 246.6455 344.4668 
posterior_scales(fit)[1, c("median", "lower", "upper")]   # the same values
#>     median    lower    upper
#> 1 246.6455 180.7061 344.4668

# A stored NUTS fit in which the scale varies among years
annual <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bayesian-annual-example.rds",
                              package = "multiScaleR"))$fits$pooled
year_term <- annual$specification$scales$habitat$random$year
tau <- exp(annual$draws$log_scale_sd[, year_term$sd_index])
median(tau)        # between-year SD of log sigma
#> [1] 0.2351976
median(exp(tau))   # a year one SD above typical has this multiple of sigma
#> [1] 1.265159
